Careers and Guidance
The Careers Programme is a critical aspect of our school’s commitment to equipping students with the knowledge, skills and experiences necessary to make informed decisions about their futures.Our Careers team provide high-quality careers education, information, advice and guidance (CEIAG) to motivate and inspire our students. We aim to equip them with the skills, knowledge and information needed to achieve their full potential at school, work, and ultimately throughout their career. We prepare pupils for future success in education, employment or training.We have been early adopters of the Gatsby Standards, using these recommendations and the results of our Compass Benchmarking to develop and improve our careers provision from Year 7 through to Year 11. We are performing above average against these national Benchmarks. More information about the Gatsby Benchmarks can be found here:
Good Career Guidance Report.
The Careers Programme is structured, impartial, and embedded across the whole school.We adhere to statutory guidance on careers education, including ‘Careers guidance and access for education and training providers’ and work closely with the Careers and Enterprise Company to ensure compliance with relevant legislation.Throughout our careers programme we collaborate with employers and post-16/18 learning providers including local colleges, sixth forms, universities and apprenticeship training providers. An independent Careers Advisor provides 1:1 Career Advice for our Year 11 students, ensuring every student receives bespoke support before they leave school. We work with organisations that aim to support young people in their transition from school into further learning or the workplace, including the Local Authority.Providers are invited into school to work with students through events, assemblies, tutor sessions and targeted group work. We also organise external trips to higher and further education providers.If you would like to learn more about our Careers programme or learn more about how you can get involved, please email careers@priorysouthsea.org
For Post-16 support and advice, please visit our bespoke Google site
https://sites.google.com/priorysouthsea.org/priory-yr10-post16options
o Careers education is embedded across subjects, enabling students to understand the relevance of their studies to the world of work. o Specific lessons are also delivered on employability skills, CV writing and interview preparation.
o Partnerships with local businesses, including guest speakers, industry-led workshops and workplace visits. o Mock Interview Day and annual Careers Fair featuring representatives from local industries, apprenticeship providers, colleges and universities. o Business Enterprise Adviser engagement with Astute Technology o Education Business Partnership (EBP) curriculum lessons
o Year 10 students have the opportunity to complete one-week work experience placement, providing real-world exposure and insights into workplace expectations.
o One-to-one career guidance interviews are offered to all Year 11 students with an independent qualified careers adviser
o Visits to universities and colleges, as well as talks on apprenticeships and vocational pathways. E.g. All Year 10 students are invited to experience taster days at local colleges.
EvaluationReviewing impact is a key part of what we do. We work closely with the Local Authority inproviding destinations data (also reported to our governors) and to provide intervention forstudents at risk of becoming NEET (not in education, employment, or training).The school has a nominated Governor for careers and the Local Governing Body receivesannual update on the careers programme, its value for money and its impact on all studentsand holds the School leadership to account for an effective careers programme that deliversthe best interests of all students.We formally assess our progress towards each of the 8 Gatsby Benchmarks each termusing the Compass evaluation tool as part of our partnership working with the Careers andEnterprise Company.
Interventions are implemented during each year in response to constant evaluation so that
(i) as wide a group as possible of students are informed about as wide a range ofopportunities
(ii) all students can access career paths and development opportunities regardlessof background, gender, disability or other condition or situation that mayotherwise present a barrier to such access.
Careers in the CurriculumTeaching staff and departments are aware of their important role in careers. Careers contentis embedded into lessons and staff are actively working towards improving the ‘careers inthe curriculum’ content for their subject. Increasingly, school trips aim to include LabourMarket Information and provide opportunities to engage with employers in the workplace,with an aim to inspire students about potential career pathways. National Careers Week inMarch is celebrated across the school with careers lessons in every subject in all yeargroups.We also encourage all staff to consider careers learning opportunities when running tripsand events – such as requesting speakers to share their career journeys and provide worktaster experiences.If any of our parents/carers are interested in sharing their career stories with our studentsthen please reach out to us by emailing careers@priorysouthsea.org
Useful websites for students, parents and carers
Beyond Priory – AlumniWe love hearing about the adventures of our previous students. If you’d like to share a storyabout where you are now, come in to talk to current students about your experiences thenplease email us at careers@priorysouthsea.org

Report an Absence
Regular attendance is extremely important and parents are asked to encourage their children to aim for the highest standards of attendance and punctuality. Family holidays should not be arranged in term time. Where a family holiday is taken in term time against advice with no specific return date, the pupil can be taken off roll. There is also the possibility of a penalty fine in these circumstances.
Parents are asked to telephone the school on the first day of any unavoidable absence and any subsequent day their child is absent. An absence note should also be sent in with their child on return. In the case of a long absence contact must be maintained with the school every few days.
Medical appointments, where possible, should be made outside of school hours in order to minimise disruption to learning. If an appointment is made during school hours, please ensure your child has a note on them for the time they need to sign out and an indication of the time they will be returning.
Any problems may be referred to the school’s Attendance Officer.
When absence is unexplained the school may telephone parents or send an unauthorised absence letter.
Please note that the school can issue Fixed Penalty Notices for unauthorised absence. This can entail a fine of £60 per parent.
We are also working very closely with the Portsmouth City Council to improve attendance. For more information please follow this link.

Emma
British Champion 2017 and 2018 qualified for the Great Britain Gymnastic Squad 2019
Emma began doing Gymnastics at 2 years old and has been inspired by both her mother & grandmother to take up the sport. In turn, she has inspired her siblings to take it up and her 10-year-old sister is currently ranked 3rd in GB for her age group. Emma’s coach is the first British all-star which gives her the determination to join her in the title. Emma’s specialty is Gymnastic floor work.
“I love the sport and am very motivated. After an injury last year it did knock my confidence, and it was hard to see my team progress without me, but this has made me want it more and I am determined to work hard and hopefully be selected for the Olympics”

Freya
Inspirational Young woman of Portsmouth 2019
Having lost her hair through Alopecia in 2017 Freya has been determined to not let the condition control her. She has been modeling since 2018 and most recently walked at London Kids Fashion week. In March 2019 Freya was awarded the Inspirational Young Woman of Portsmouth Prize. She is a very active member of the school community involved in the school council, is an anti-bullying ambassador, and has taken part in multiple maths challenges., she enjoys Cheerleading, dancing and is part of a Triathlon group.
“I am most proud of the fact that I have been able to inspire people of all ages who have felt self-conscious about the way they look and I hope to continue to do so.”

Priory School Shortlisted for The Economist Foundation’s Leadership for Change Prize 2025
Priory School, part of the high-achieving Bohunt Education Trust, is delighted to announce that its students have been shortlisted for The Economist Foundation’s prestigious Leadership for Change Prize 2025, placing among the top 11 projects out of more than 120 entries nationwide.
The shortlisting recognises the exceptional creativity, dedication, and impact of Priory’s students. The project caught the attention of journalists from The Economist and The Guardian, who praised the calibre of work submitted.
Helen Blachford, Trust Subject Director of Personal Development and Curriculum Leader for Citizenship & PSHE, said:“I am incredibly proud of our students for reaching the final 11. Their commitment and enthusiasm throughout this project have been outstanding, and this recognition reflects the hard work and leadership they have shown.”
Neil Strowger, Trust Leader at Bohunt Education Trust, added:“This is a remarkable achievement for Priory School. Being shortlisted in such a competitive national competition is a testament to the dedication of both staff and students in fostering leadership, creativity, and a commitment to making a positive difference in the world.”
As part of the recognition, Priory School will receive certificates celebrating the achievement and will be featured on The Economist Foundation’s website and in its curated magazine. Additionally, the School has been invited to participate in the Topical Talk Festival in January 2026, a global initiative designed to engage students with contemporary news topics and discussions.
Georgia & Raphaela

Matthew
Junior Player for London Irish Rugby Club.
Matthew has played for Portsmouth Rugby Club but has been particularly busy. this season he was lucky enough to be one of only 50 players scouted by London Irish Rugby Club. Since then he has trained three times a week with the club, with matches on top of that. He hopes to play professionally after school, and is taking BTEC PE to help keep his fitness levels up alongside training.
“I love Rugby because I have played it since a young age, and I love the physical side of training and the game, as it is a high energy game that keeps your fitness up. I respect players like Owen Farrell and Johnny May because of their quick feet and style of play.

Ruby
Charity Fundraising through Physical Challenges
Over the last 4 years, Ruby has raised over £1000 for Cancer research by Undertaking a Triathlon in 2016 and a 250m Freefall abseiling down the orbit in London in 2019.
Ruby is a competitive sportswoman and since first signing for Southampton Football Club, she has played for Portsmouth and reading. She has also been called up on multiple occasions to play for the Welsh national team to compete across the world. Despite suffering injuries which mean there were periods where she could not train, Ruby, remains completely committed to her sports & fundraising. Ruby is also a member of the school student leadership and a keen environmental activist.

Headteacher’s Welcome
Priory School is a fantastic place to work and learn. We are a thriving, vibrant and energetic community demonstrating a common purpose – to ensure the very best for each and every one of our students. We are a school with a distinct ethos that recognises every student has their own individual strengths, gifts and talents; our aim is to ensure that these are all developed to their full potential. We look for excellence in all aspects of learning. I hope you find our website informative and gain a real insight into the amazing experiences and successes of our students.
I believe Priory School is a truly excellent school; it is a place where staff are committed and proud to work, a place which Governors and parents, carers and guardians are proud to support and a school to which students are proud to belong.
We lead and innovate to make learning challenging and distinctive. Therelationships between teachers, students, parents and guardians are fundamentalto the success of the school. Working together we ensure that students enjoytheir time at Priory, make progress above the national average and leave us asresponsible, well-qualified, mature young people; ready to make a valuedcontribution to society. Providing top quality teaching and learning, in orderthat all students can improve their academic and personal outcomes and achievetheir full potential, remains at the heart of all that we do.
We are committed to enabling all our young people to develop into happy, tolerant and confident adults; treating others like they would wish to be treated themselves. Our school community is friendly, but disciplined with our students understanding the value of hard work as the backbone of achieving success whilst embracing all that is best in respect of the new technologies.
This is a successful school where we aspire for everyone to improve on their personal best with a relentless pursuit of excellence. We never rest on our laurels, but look for new opportunities so that we continue to inspire confident and independent learners who are equipped for, and will thrive in, a changing world.
I trust that during your visit to our website you find much to illustrate the depth of opportunity that exists at this Priory. If you are a prospective parent, we would like to invite you to visit our school to form your own judgement. Please contact us at priory@priorysouthsea.org and will be happy to arrange this for you.
Thank you for your interest in our school.

Governors
Each Bohunt school has a local governing board which reports directly to the Bohunt trust board on a regular basis. Governors carry out key functions in supporting schools, working closely with headteachers to:
The local governing board offers strategic support and guidance to school leaders enabling young people to fulfil their potential and achieve their aspirations. They consistently challenge processes and drive continuous school improvement having a significant role in the long-term development and improvement of the school and provide strong links with the wider community.
If you are interested in being a governor at a BET school, please submit your details via our online Expression of Interest form and a member of the Governance Team will contact you with further details.
If you would like to contact the Local Governing Board, please email the Trust Governance Lead at staylor1@bohunt.hants.sch.uk

Support for Learning
At Priory School we believe that pupils have a right to an education which is appropriate to their needs and abilities as individuals. As far as possible it is our aim to identify and minimise any barriers to learning or specific difficulties that pupils may or do experience.
The team is dedicated to making sure all of our pupils have the best possible outcomes in their education and into adulthood. We balance support with promoting independence. We are always working towards preparing our pupils for adulthood. The department works alongside teaching staff to enable all pupils to access a broad and balanced curriculum.
The pupil support department works with pupils according to their individual needs to ensure that all pupils, including those with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) make good progress. Support takes a number of forms; it may be given individually or in small groups, in mainstream classes or within the pupil support department. We are sensitive to the emotional needs of our young people and ensure that pupils are not isolated or stigmatised when working with the department
We aim to provide short term interventions that enable pupils to be successful independent learners in the classroom. Some pupils, who have more complex needs will require longer-term or more specialist support from the department, this will be tailored to their individual needs.
